appraisal_events.evidence: Mme Verdurin ne commençait jamais un article de Brichot sans la satisfaction préalable de penser qu'elle allait y trouver des choses ridicules... 'moi je trouve ça écrit comme par un cochon'... Puis se moquer de lui devint une mode comme ç'avait été de l'admirer.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin orchestrates a sustained campaign of ridicule against Brichot's wartime journalism, turning fashionable admiration of him into fashionable mockery across her salon and the wider social world.

appraisal_events.evidence: le couple charmant avait souri, tourné Norpois en ridicule, cité des preuves de son gâtisme et conclu qu'il avait dit cela... devant M. Caillaux narquois.
appraisal_events.explanation: An English couple mocks Norpois directly and treats his confident pronouncement about Caillaux as evidence of senile decline, discrediting him in front of the duc de Guermantes.

appraisal_events.evidence: il fallait voir les moments de silence et d'hésitation qu'avait Mme de Forcheville... avant de dire, sur le ton d'un sentiment intime... Pour prononcer «le cran»... elle faisait avec sa main le geste de pétrissage et avec ses yeux le clignement des rapins.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironizes Odette's performance of having independent opinions, exposing her pronouncements and anglophile mannerisms as borrowed and imitative rather than genuine.

status_effects.explanation: Brichot's public standing collapses from admired 'grand homme' of the salons to a figure mocked by both the Verdurin circle and, eventually, fashionable society at large.
Mme Verdurin successfully directs the opinion of her circle and eventually the wider Faubourg Saint-Germain against Brichot, demonstrating her continuing social and rhetorical control.
Norpois's credibility is undercut when he is publicly ridiculed and associated with senility, though this is reported as a single, fairly isolated incident.
Odette's attempt to appear independently opinionated is undercut by narratorial irony revealing her views and mannerisms as derivative and performative.

ambiguities: The passage refers to Odette as 'Mme de Forcheville', a form not listed among her aliases in the alias map; identity is confirmed by the explicit adjacent use of 'Odette' and the reference to her son-in-law Saint-Loup, but the mapping required contextual inference.

The mockery of Norpois is partly relayed through Charlus's own self-satisfied, narrator-criticized rant, so it is uncertain how much of the negative judgment of Norpois reflects narratorial endorsement versus Charlus's own unreliable bias.
